label: PrimeNG
notes: PrimeNG binds values with [(ngModel)]; jig controls use a signal `value` model — migrate `[(ngModel)]="x"` to `[(value)]="x"` (or reactive forms via jig-input-field). PrimeNG form controls are usually standalone; jig form controls are typically wrapped in `jig-input-field` for label/hint/error chrome. Icons are set via `icon*` inputs (e.g. `iconDropdown`) or projected `jig-icon`, not template slots. Always verify target inputs with get_control before rewriting.

Import JigTableModule from `@awdlab/jig/table`. Same two-template shape as PrimeNG: `<ng-template #header>` holds `<tr jigTableHeadTr>` with `<th [jigTableTh]="table.column('field')">` cells, `<ng-template #body let-row [jigTemplate]="table.templateTypes.body">` holds `<tr [jigTableBodyTr]="row">` with `<td jigTableTd>` cells; the row object is `row.data`. Features are per-column directives on the `th` (sort, filter, sticky). Data is filtered and sorted client-side unless `filterLocally` / `sortLocally` are `false` or a `dataSource` is set. Give the table a fixed height; it scrolls its body itself.

gaps: No `rows` / `rowsPerPageOptions` / `[(first)]` inputs — the paginator owns page size and index (persist them through `storage`).
No row expansion (`pRowToggler` / `#expandedrow`), cell editing (`pEditableColumn`) or export (`exportCSV`) — build these in your row templates.
No global filter (`filterGlobal` / `globalFilterFields`) — filter `rows` yourself or use column filters.
